blocks.text: Condo buildings in College Park PM
Westhill Place — 200 and 204 Westhill Place

The sub-area's one verified apartment-condo complex: one complex across two addresses (the building directory entry is for 204 Westhill Place), a wood-frame apartment building in College Park PM per the directory and current listings. The directory's listing header records 150 units; the directory records built 1973, while current listings record build years of 1970 and 1974 for units in the complex. The directory records its restrictions as: pets allowed with restrictions, rentals allowed with restrictions — the rental-restriction element of that line is void since November 24, 2022. Current listings describe the form as Apartment/Condo, with heat and hot water included in the strata fee, an indoor pool, exercise room and community garden, and cats OK.
Streets, schools and getting around College Park PM

items.t: College Park is an established south-side Port Moody neighbourhood between Clarke Road and the Barnet Highway corridor, under College Park Way and Princeton Avenue, between Seaview to the west and Glenayre / Moody Centre to the east.

Where condo stock concentrates: College Park's verified attached shelf is Westhill Place at the south end of the neighbourhood (200 and 204 Westhill Place) and the townhouse complexes on Seaview Drive and Clarke Road in. SnapStats GVR September 2026 report.
Transit: buses connect College Park to Moody Centre Station, which pairs the Millennium Line Evergreen Extension with the West Coast Express downtown.

Schools and catchments: Port Moody is served by SD43 Coquitlam and catchments are address-based — confirm a specific address in the district's catchment tools. Schools operating in this part of Port Moody include Glenayre Elementary and Seaview Community School, with Moody Middle School and Port Moody Secondary serving central Port Moody.
Recreation and civic facilities: Glenayre Centre, 492 Glencoe Drive; Port Moody Recreation Complex, 300 Ioco Road; Port Moody Public Library, 100 Newport Drive.
Health: Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, is in Port Moody itself (east of this area); Royal Columbian Hospital in New Westminster is the larger regional hospital.

items.t: Port Moody property taxes: due July 2, 2026; a 5% penalty applies after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% penalty after September 15, 2026. Utility fees are billed separately; the 2026 utility bill was due February 27, 2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about College Park PM

items.t: Port Moody replaced its Official Community Plan this year, and the old number is everywhere. OCP Bylaw 2026, No. 3522 was adopted April 28, 2026 and repeals OCP Bylaw No. 2955; listing packages and older guides still cite 2955. Any zoning or OCP argument for a College Park purchase should run off 3522.

The one condo building cannot agree with itself on when it was built. Westhill Place's sources give 1970, 1973 and 1974 across its directory entry and listings — a fifty-year-old wood-frame complex where the depreciation report, not the listing sheet, is the document that matters.

A name collision crosses two cities and two tenures. Cedar Ridge (70 Seaview Dr, Port Moody — 28 freehold townhomes, completed 2020, no age restriction) sits one shortened name away from Cedar Creek Estates (3031 200 St, Township of Langley — a verified 55+ pad-rental manufactured-home park). A feed that truncates names can present a Port Moody townhome as a Langley seniors park; check the civic address and tenure, not the label.
Aggregator neighbourhood labels put buildings in College Park that their own listings put elsewhere.
The sub-area's "future seniors housing" is neither in the sub-area nor seniors stock. Westport Village's Phase 2 seniors tower is a Moody Centre presale concept on the presale source.

A school building stands in the neighbourhood that the district's list does not confirm. The College Park Elementary building at 300 Princeton Avenue does not appear in SD43's current Port Moody school list — a buyer assuming an in-neighbourhood elementary catchment from the building's presence would be assuming; catchments here are address-based and must be checked.

items.t: Port Moody community figures: detached median $1,685,000, $608/sq ft, 96% sale-to-list, 33 days; attached median $715,000, $666/sq ft, 94% sale-to-list, 29 days.

Schools: SD43 Coquitlam, catchments address-based and to be checked in the SD43 School Locator by exact address. SD43 schools in this part of Port Moody include Glenayre Elementary and Seaview Community School (Ministry-listed names: Ecole Glenayre Elementary, 495 Glencoe Dr; Seaview Community School, 1215 Cecile Dr), with Ecole Moody Middle and Port Moody Secondary serving central Port Moody.

Transit and roads: Barnet Highway (Highway 7A) and St. Johns Street run east–west through the city toward Burnaby and Coquitlam; Moody Centre and Inlet Centre stations are the city's two SkyTrain stops, and TransLink buses connect west Port Moody to Moody Centre Station (Millennium Line Evergreen Extension and West Coast Express).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in College Park PM

items.t: Form B diligence (every College Park strata): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

City plan: Port Moody Official Community Plan Bylaw 2026, No. 3522, adopted April 28, 2026, repeals Bylaw No. 2955. Chapter 14 sets policy for the city's neighbourhoods; the Suncor refinery lands beside College Park and Seaview are designated a Special Study Area in the OCP — the main planning item hanging over this end of the city, and a disclosure item on any College Park purchase.

City zoning and SSMUH: Zoning Bylaw 2018, No. 2937 puts single detached homes in RS zones and multi-residential homes in RT and RM zones. Under Bylaw Amendment No. 94, 2024, No. 3460, small-scale multi-unit housing is permitted in RS and RT zones outside the transit-oriented areas (the TOAs are exempt from the SSMUH rules): up to four units on lots from 280 m² to 4,050 m², and up to six units within 400 m of frequent bus stops. Trap specific to this sub-area: the RS1-S small-lot subdivision standard (minimum 9 m width, 325 m²) is available only in Moody Centre, Seaview and Pleasantside OCP Single Family–Low Density areas — College Park is not on that list, so do not price a College Park lot off the small-lot offer; confirm any split idea with the City. Environmentally sensitive area and hazardous lands / steep slope development permit areas (DPA 4 and DPA 5) apply in parts of the area, watercourse lots need riparian assessment under Zoning Bylaw s. 5.4, and no floodplain or ALR land is confirmed in College Park.

blocks.text: Good to know about College Park PM

items.t: Two Clarke Road addresses, two opposite tenures, 150 metres of confusion. A street-name search alone will merge them.

Port Moody replaced its OCP in 2026, and the old number is still everywhere. Bylaw 2026, No. 3522 was adopted April 28, 2026 and repeals Bylaw No. 2955 — any guide or listing package still citing 2955 as the current OCP is a bylaw out of date.
The sub-area's namesake school may not be a school anymore.
The refinery next door is the area's open planning question.

The "retirement residence" in search results is in Saskatchewan. "College Park Retirement Residence" resolves to College Park II in Regina — there is no such building in Port Moody, and the city has zero verified 55+ ownership stock of any form.

blocks.text: College Park home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

27 townhomes sold in College Park with a median price of $829,000 (the middle half sold between $765,000 and $883,500), taking a median of 26 days to sell at 98.4% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $485 per square foot, a median year built of 1977 and a median strata fee of $626 a month. 8 condos sold in College Park with a median price of $487,500 (the middle half sold between $412,500 and $542,500), taking a median of 40 days to sell at 98.2% of the last list price; 12% sold above list. They had a median $505 per square foot, a median year built of 1976 and a median strata fee of $437 a month.

faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 14 condos and townhomes listed in College Park. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.
faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in College Park?

faq.a: In October 2026, condos and townhomes in College Park had a sales ratio of 14%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.
faq.q: Is College Park a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?

faq.a: 18 condos and townhomes sold in College Park over those 5 months, out of 174 in all of Port Moody.
faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in College Park from June to October 2026?

faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.
faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?

faq.a: One verified by name: Westhill Place (200 and 204 Westhill Place, 150 units per the building directory's listing header, early-1970s wood-frame). The rest of the named attached shelf is townhouses (Stone Ridge, Cedar Ridge, Clarke Townhomes).
faq.q: How many apartment-condo buildings does College Park have?

faq.a: There is no 55+ strata, rental or retirement residence verified inside this sub-area at all, and the "College Park Retirement Residence" appearing in searches is in Regina, Saskatchewan. Do not let the word "Park" or an aggregator's neighbourhood label imply otherwise.
faq.q: Is there any 55+ condo I can buy in College Park?

faq.a: No. Westport Village is a presale at Clarke Street & Douglas Street in Moody Centre (not College Park); its 12-storey seniors housing tower is a future Phase 2. It is future product, not stock, anywhere.
faq.q: Westport Village advertises a seniors tower — can I buy into it now?

faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC, including the restriction element in Westhill Place's directory line.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Westhill Place unit?

faq.a: Current listings state that heat and hot water are included in the strata fee, with an indoor pool, exercise room and community garden on site. Confirm the current inclusions and fee against the Form B — the complex's directories and listings disagree on its build year (1970, 1973 and 1974 all appear), so verify everything against strata documents.
faq.q: What is actually included in the Westhill Place strata fee?

faq.a: No. Fresh listing evidence records its Title to Land as Freehold Strata, with a monthly maintenance fee — "freehold" there means freehold strata title, the standard BC strata title. There is a Form B, a depreciation report and strata fees, exactly as at any strata.
faq.q: Cedar Ridge is advertised as "freehold townhomes" — does that mean no strata?
What did townhomes in College Park sell for?
faq.a: 27 townhomes sold in College Park between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $829,000.

faq.q: How long do townhomes take to sell in College Park?
faq.a: The median was 26 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 98.4% of the last list price (0% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
